tools.name: Apply a database migration

inputs.name: name

inputs.name: query

inputs.name: rollback
inputs.about: Optional SQL query to rollback/undo this migration if needed.

inputs.name: idempotency_key
inputs.about: A unique key to ensure the same migration is tracked only once. If provided, prevents duplicate migrations with the same key from being applied.

tools.description: Activates a vanity subdomain for the specified Supabase project (e.g., 'my-brand.supabase.co'). Important notes: - Vanity subdomains require a paid plan (Pro/Team/Enterprise) - Usage of vanity subdomains and custom domains is mutually exclusive - After activation, your project's auth services will no longer work on the original {project-ref}.supabase.co hostname - Schedule a downtime window to update client code and OAuth providers before activating

inputs.name: vanity_subdomain

tools.name: Authorize user through OAuth
tools.description: Requests Supabase OAuth 2.0 authorization for a registered application and returns the redirect location when the endpoint responds with a redirect, or status and error information otherwise.

inputs.name: scope
inputs.about: Space-separated list of OAuth scopes for requested permissions on user resources (e.g., 'email profile', 'storage.objects.read').

inputs.name: state
inputs.about: Opaque value to maintain state between request and callback; returned unmodified to aid CSRF prevention.

inputs.name: client_id
inputs.about: Unique identifier for the OAuth client application, registered with Supabase. Must be a valid client_id from a registered OAuth application.

inputs.name: redirect_uri
inputs.about: URI where Supabase redirects the user after authorization; must exactly match a registered URI for the client application.

inputs.name: response_mode
inputs.about: Specifies how authorization response parameters are returned (e.g., 'query', 'fragment', 'form_post'). Default is determined by `response_type` if not specified.

inputs.name: response_type
inputs.about: Specifies the authorization flow type: 'code' for Authorization Code Grant; 'token' for Implicit Grant (access token); 'id_token token' for OIDC hybrid flows (ID and access tokens).

inputs.name: code_challenge
inputs.about: PKCE code challenge to secure authorization code grants, typically a BASE64URL-encoded SHA256 hash of `code_verifier`.

inputs.name: code_challenge_method
inputs.about: Method to derive `code_challenge` for PKCE: 'S256'/'sha256' for SHA256 hashing; 'plain' sends verifier as is (not for production if hashing possible). Required if `code_challenge` is provided.

inputs.name: read_replica_region

inputs.name: ipv4_addresses

inputs.name: database_identifier

tools.description: Executes PostgreSQL queries against a Supabase project's database for data retrieval, modification, or schema operations. Read-only mode does not prevent detected INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE statements from making changes.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.about: The unique reference ID of the Supabase project (used in the URL path). Must be exactly 20 lowercase letters (a-z). Can be found in Project Settings > General > Reference ID in the Supabase Dashboard, or from the dashboard URL: https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/<project-ref>. Can also be provid

inputs.name: read_only
inputs.about: If true, executes the query in a read-only transaction. Useful for safety when only fetching data without modifying the database. IMPORTANT: This parameter is incompatible with data modification statements. For INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements, if set to true, it will be automatically overridde

tools.name: Beta update project network restrictions

tools.name: Count action runs
tools.description: Counts the number of action runs for a Supabase project using a HEAD request. Use this when you need to retrieve the total count of action runs without fetching the full list of runs.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.about: The unique reference ID (20 alphanumeric characters) of your Supabase project. You can find this in your project's dashboard URL or by calling the List All Projects action.

tools.name: Count Function Results
tools.description: Count rows from a known exposed table-valued function using HEAD, without a body. PostgREST enforces a read-only transaction; functions attempting database writes fail. Uses an elevated secret/service_role key that bypasses Row Level Security. OAuth requires secrets:read; fine-grained PATs require api_gateway_keys_read and api_gateway_keys_secret_read for project-key discovery. Not for scalar functions.

inputs.name: count
inputs.about: Count strategy: exact (default) may be slow on large results; planned uses PostgreSQL statistics; estimated uses exact below the server's db-max-rows threshold and planned above it.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Optional page size; does not limit the total matching-row count.

inputs.name: order
inputs.about: PostgREST result ordering, e.g. created_at.desc.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.about: Optional page offset; does not subtract from the total count.

inputs.name: schema
inputs.about: Exposed schema sent as Accept-Profile; omit for the default schema.

inputs.name: select
inputs.about: PostgREST column/embedded-resource selection, e.g. id,name.

inputs.name: filters
inputs.about: PostgREST result filters, e.g. {'rating': 'gt.8'} or {'or': '(rating.gt.8,featured.is.true)'}. Do not include query controls or names used in arguments.

inputs.name: arguments
inputs.about: Named function arguments as PostgreSQL query-literal strings, e.g. {'minimum': '10', 'ids': '{1,2,3}'}. Values are URL-encoded by the transport, not JSON-serialized. Omit for a function without arguments. Argument names cannot overlap filters or PostgREST query controls.

inputs.name: project_ref
inputs.about: Unique 20-character reference ID of the Supabase project.

inputs.name: function_name
inputs.about: Name of the exposed, read-only table-valued Postgres function.

tools.name: Count Table Rows
tools.description: Count matching rows in an exposed table or view without downloading rows. Uses an elevated secret/service-role key and bypasses Row Level Security. OAuth requires secrets:read; fine-grained personal access tokens require api_gateway_keys_read and api_gateway_keys_secret_read.

inputs.name: count
inputs.about: Count strategy: exact counts all matches and may be slow on large tables; planned uses PostgreSQL statistics; estimated uses exact below the server's row threshold and planned above it.

inputs.name: limit
inputs.about: Page size, including zero. Does not cap the matching-row total.

inputs.name: order
inputs.about: PostgREST ordering expression, for example created_at.desc.

inputs.name: table
inputs.about: Name of an exposed table or view, without a schema prefix.

inputs.name: offset
inputs.about: Rows to skip for the requested page, not the matching-row total.

inputs.name: schema
inputs.about: Exposed schema to select through Accept-Profile; omit for the default schema.

inputs.name: select
inputs.about: PostgREST column and embedded-resource selection, for example id,name.

inputs.name: filters
inputs.about: PostgREST filters mapping columns or logical operators to expressions, for example {'status': 'eq.active', 'or': '(age.lt.18,age.gt.65)'}. Use the dedicated fields for select, order, limit, and offset.

inputs.name: project_ref
inputs.about: Unique 20-character reference ID of the Supabase project.

tools.name: Update project's postgres config
tools.description: Updates specified PostgreSQL configuration parameters for an existing Supabase project (`ref`) to optimize database performance; note that unspecified parameters remain unchanged, and caution is advised as incorrect settings can impact stability or require a restart.

inputs.name: ref
inputs.about: The unique reference ID of the Supabase project.

inputs.name: work_mem
inputs.about: Memory for internal sorts and hash tables before writing to temp disk files (e.g., '4MB', '64MB').

inputs.name: max_wal_size
inputs.about: WAL size that triggers a checkpoint (e.g., '1GB', '2048MB').

inputs.name: wal_keep_size
inputs.about: Minimum size of past WAL log segments in pg_wal for standby servers (e.g., '128MB', '512MB'); replaces older wal_keep_segments.

inputs.name: shared_buffers
inputs.about: Memory for shared memory buffers (e.g., '128MB', '1GB').

inputs.name: max_connections
inputs.about: Maximum concurrent database connections. Typically between 1 and 262143.

inputs.name: statement_timeout
inputs.about: Maximum allowed duration for any SQL statement (e.g., '10000ms', '30s'); '0' typically disables timeout.

inputs.name: effective_cache_size
inputs.about: Estimated disk cache size for a single query (e.g., '4GB', '512MB').

inputs.name: maintenance_work_mem
inputs.about: Maximum memory for maintenance operations like VACUUM, CREATE INDEX (e.g., '64MB', '1GB').

inputs.name: max_parallel_workers
inputs.about: Maximum workers the system can support for parallel queries. Typically between 0 and 1024.

inputs.name: max_worker_processes
inputs.about: Maximum background processes the system can support. Typically between 0 and 262143.

inputs.name: max_slot_wal_keep_size
inputs.about: Maximum WAL file size replication slots can retain in pg_wal (e.g., '1GB', '512MB'). '0' might mean unlimited; check PostgreSQL docs.

inputs.name: session_replication_role
inputs.about: Controls firing of replication-related triggers and rules for the current session.

inputs.name: max_locks_per_transaction
inputs.about: Controls the average number of object locks allocated per transaction. Typically between 10 and 2147483640.

inputs.name: max_standby_archive_delay
inputs.about: Maximum delay before canceling queries on a hot standby server processing archived WAL data (e.g., '30s', '0ms' to disable).

inputs.name: max_standby_streaming_delay
inputs.about: Maximum delay before canceling queries on a hot standby server processing streamed WAL data (e.g., '30s', '0ms' to disable).

inputs.name: max_parallel_workers_per_gather
inputs.about: Maximum workers for a single Gather or Gather Merge node in a parallel query. Typically between 0 and 1024.

inputs.name: max_parallel_maintenance_workers
inputs.about: Maximum parallel processes for a single maintenance utility command. Typically between 0 and 1024.

tools.name: Update Table Rows
tools.description: Update matching rows in an exposed Supabase table or updatable view. Uses a secret or service_role project key, bypassing Row Level Security. PostgREST warns that unfiltered PATCH updates every row: filters are required unless allow_all_rows=true. Filters can still match every row; check them carefully. OAuth needs secrets:read; fine-grained PATs need api_gateway_keys_read and api_gateway_keys_secret_read to reveal the project key.

inputs.name: count
inputs.about: Optional PostgREST count strategy. Exact counts may be expensive.

inputs.name: table
inputs.about: Exposed table or updatable view name, without a schema prefix.

inputs.name: schema
inputs.about: Exposed database schema for Content-Profile; omit for the server default.

inputs.name: select
inputs.about: PostgREST columns/embedded resources to return with returning=representation.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.about: Comma-separated payload column names to update; other payload keys are ignored. Omit to update the keys in updates. Listed keys absent from updates may be set to null.

inputs.name: filters
inputs.about: PostgREST filters, e.g. {'id': 'eq.42', 'age': 'lt.13'} or {'or': '(id.eq.1,id.eq.2)'}. Multiple keys are ANDed. Embedded-resource filters alone do not constrain target rows. Broad filters may match every row.

inputs.name: updates
inputs.about: JSON object mapping column names to new values, applied to every matching row. Explicit null sets a column to SQL NULL; omitted keys are not updated unless included explicitly in columns.

inputs.name: returning
inputs.about: PostgREST return preference: representation returns updated rows; minimal returns no body. Omit to use the server default (minimal).

inputs.name: project_ref
inputs.about: Unique 20-character reference ID of the Supabase project.

inputs.name: allow_all_rows
inputs.about: Explicitly permit an update without target-row filters. Defaults to false to prevent accidental full-table updates, as warned by PostgREST. Set true only when intentionally updating every row.
